events.event_description: Founds Laugh-O-Gram Studio in Kansas City
events.evidence_text: Disney established the Laugh-O-Gram Studio in Kansas City in May 1921.

events.event_description: Laugh-O-Gram Studio goes bankrupt
events.evidence_text: The Kansas City studio went bankrupt in 1923, sending Disney to Hollywood.

events.event_description: Co-founds Disney Brothers Studio with brother Roy
events.evidence_text: Walt and Roy formed Disney Brothers Studio, forerunner of The Walt Disney Company.

events.event_description: Marries Lillian Bounds in Lewiston, Idaho
events.evidence_text: Disney married ink artist Lillian Bounds in July 1925.

events.event_description: Loses Oswald the Lucky Rabbit rights and most staff to Charles Mintz
events.evidence_text: Dispute with distributor Mintz cost Disney the Oswald series and most animators.

events.event_description: Steamboat Willie premieres, launching Mickey Mouse
events.evidence_text: Synchronized-sound cartoon Steamboat Willie made Mickey Mouse a hit in 1928.

events.event_description: Suffers a nervous breakdown from overwork
events.evidence_text: Disney had a nervous breakdown in October 1931 and took a rest trip.

events.event_description: Daughter Diane born
events.evidence_text: First daughter Diane was born in December 1933.

events.event_description: Adopts daughter Sharon
events.evidence_text: The Disneys adopted daughter Sharon in December 1936.

events.event_description: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premieres to huge success
events.evidence_text: First full-length cel-animated feature became a major box-office success.

events.event_description: Special Academy Award for Snow White (one statuette plus seven miniatures)
events.evidence_text: Academy gave a Special Award for Snow White, presented by Shirley Temple.

events.event_description: Pinocchio and Fantasia underperform; studio sinks into heavy debt
events.evidence_text: Pinocchio and Fantasia lost money; studio deeply in debt by early 1941.

events.event_description: Five-week animators strike at the Disney studio
events.evidence_text: Animators struck for five weeks in 1941, damaging Disney's reputation.

events.event_description: Disneyland opens in Anaheim, California
events.evidence_text: Disneyland theme park opened in Anaheim in July 1955.

events.event_description: Diagnosed with lung cancer (died December 1966)
events.evidence_text: Lung cancer was found in early November 1966; he died December 15.

events.event_description: Becomes licensed milliner, opens Chanel Modes at 21 rue Cambon, Paris
events.evidence_text: Licensed as milliner in 1910, she opened Chanel Modes on rue Cambon.

events.event_description: Opens boutique in Deauville financed by Arthur Capel
events.evidence_text: A Deauville boutique opened in 1913 with Capel's financing.

events.event_description: Opens couture establishment in Biarritz
events.evidence_text: She opened an establishment in Biarritz in 1915.

events.event_description: Registered as couturiere; establishes maison de couture at 31 rue Cambon
events.evidence_text: In 1919 she registered as couturiere and set up at 31 rue Cambon.

events.event_description: Launches Chanel No. 5 perfume
events.evidence_text: Chanel No. 5 was introduced in 1921 and became world-famous.

events.event_description: Forms Parfums Chanel with the Wertheimer brothers (keeps 10% stake)
events.evidence_text: She agreed with the Wertheimers to create Parfums Chanel in 1924.

events.event_description: Closes her shops at the outbreak of World War II
events.evidence_text: She closed her shops in 1939 when the war began.

events.event_description: Interrogated by Free French purge committee over wartime collaboration
events.evidence_text: Questioned about collaboration in September 1944, then released without charge.

events.event_description: Moves into self-imposed exile in Switzerland
events.evidence_text: She moved to Switzerland in 1945.

events.event_description: Renegotiates perfume deal: royalty on No. 5 sales and living expenses covered
events.evidence_text: New Wertheimer deal gave her a share of No. 5 sales for life.

events.event_description: Reopens couture house at age 71, financed by Pierre Wertheimer
events.evidence_text: She revived her couture house in 1954 with Wertheimer financing.

events.event_description: Comeback collection panned by French press
events.evidence_text: French critics initially dismissed the 1954 comeback show.

events.event_description: Broadway musical Coco about her life opens
events.evidence_text: Musical Coco opened December 1969, closing October 1970.

events.event_description: Marries Julia Nye
events.evidence_text: Turner married Julia Nye in 1960; they divorced in 1964.

events.event_description: Takes over family billboard company after father's suicide
events.evidence_text: At 24 he became president of the family advertising firm in 1963.

events.event_description: Divorces Julia Nye
events.evidence_text: First marriage to Julia Nye ended in divorce in 1964.

events.event_description: Marries Jane Smith
events.evidence_text: He married Jane Smith in 1965; they divorced in 1988.

events.event_description: Buys Atlanta UHF station WJRJ (later WTCG), start of Turner Broadcasting
events.evidence_text: Purchase of an Atlanta UHF station began Turner Broadcasting System.

events.event_description: Buys the Atlanta Braves; WTCG goes national as cable superstation (Dec 17)
events.evidence_text: He bought the Braves in 1976; WTCG became a national superstation.

events.event_description: Skippers Courageous to win the America's Cup
events.evidence_text: Turner won the 1977 America's Cup as skipper of Courageous.

events.event_description: Launches CNN, first 24-hour cable news channel
events.evidence_text: CNN debuted June 1, 1980 as the first 24-hour news channel.

events.event_description: Failed hostile takeover attempt of CBS
events.evidence_text: His attempt to acquire CBS did not succeed.

events.event_description: Buys MGM/UA for $1.5 billion, leaving heavy debt; forced to sell parts back
events.evidence_text: MGM purchase left heavy debt; he sold parts back to Kerkorian.

events.event_description: Divorces Jane Smith
events.evidence_text: Second marriage to Jane Smith ended in 1988.

events.event_description: Marries actress Jane Fonda
events.evidence_text: Turner married Jane Fonda in December 1991.

events.event_description: Turner Broadcasting merges with Time Warner; becomes vice chairman and top shareholder
events.evidence_text: Turner Broadcasting merged into Time Warner in October 1996.

events.event_description: AOL-Time Warner stock collapse costs him up to $7 billion; divorce from Fonda the same year
events.evidence_text: Turner estimated losing as much as $7 billion after the AOL merger.

events.event_description: Resigns as AOL Time Warner vice chairman
events.evidence_text: He resigned as vice chairman of AOL Time Warner in 2003.

events.event_description: Moves to WJZ-TV Baltimore to co-anchor the evening news
events.evidence_text: She joined Baltimore's WJZ-TV as six o'clock news co-anchor in 1976.

events.event_description: Takes over AM Chicago on WLS-TV
events.evidence_text: Her first AM Chicago episode aired January 2, 1984.

events.event_description: Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress (The Color Purple)
events.evidence_text: The Color Purple earned her an Academy Award nomination.

events.event_description: Founds Harpo Productions as chairwoman and CEO
events.evidence_text: She became chairwoman and CEO of Harpo Productions in 1986.

events.event_description: The Oprah Winfrey Show goes national in syndication
events.evidence_text: The show was first broadcast nationwide on September 8, 1986.

events.event_description: Jury finds her not liable in Texas cattlemen beef-defamation suit
events.evidence_text: A jury found Winfrey and Lyman not liable on February 26, 1998.

events.event_description: Self-produced film Beloved flops, losing about $30 million
events.evidence_text: Beloved opened poorly in October 1998, losing about $30 million.

events.event_description: Named by Forbes the first Black woman billionaire
events.evidence_text: Forbes named her the first Black woman billionaire in 2003.

events.event_description: Book-club pick A Million Little Pieces exposed as fabricated; public backlash
events.evidence_text: After fabrications surfaced she confronted author James Frey on air.

events.event_description: Launches Oprah Winfrey Network (OWN) after delay
events.evidence_text: OWN launched January 1, 2011, delayed from a planned 2009 debut.

events.event_description: Ends The Oprah Winfrey Show after 25 seasons
events.evidence_text: The series finale aired May 25, 2011.

events.event_description: Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom
events.evidence_text: President Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013.

events.event_description: Buys about 10% stake in Weight Watchers; shares surge
events.evidence_text: Her stake purchase in Weight Watchers sent its shares sharply higher.

events.event_description: Marries Mildred Williams
events.evidence_text: Hefner married Mildred Williams in 1949.

events.event_description: Daughter Christie born
events.evidence_text: Daughter Christie was born in 1952.

events.event_description: Launches Playboy magazine (first issue December 1953)
events.evidence_text: He launched Playboy, first issue dated December 1953.

events.event_description: Son David born
events.evidence_text: Son David was born in 1955.

events.event_description: Divorces Mildred Williams
events.evidence_text: His first marriage ended in divorce in 1959.

events.event_description: Opens first Playboy Club in Chicago
events.evidence_text: The first Playboy Club opened in Chicago in 1960.

events.event_description: Arrested for obscenity over nude photos; trial ends in hung jury
events.evidence_text: Arrested June 4, 1963 for obscene literature; jury deadlocked.

events.event_description: Playboy Enterprises goes public; buys Playboy Mansion West
events.evidence_text: Playboy Enterprises became publicly traded in 1971.

events.event_description: Suffers a stroke at age 58
events.evidence_text: Hefner had a minor stroke on March 7, 1985.

events.event_description: Steps back; daughter Christie takes over Playboy operations
events.evidence_text: Christie Hefner took over the company's operations in 1988.

events.event_description: Marries Kimberley Conrad
events.evidence_text: He married Playmate Kimberley Conrad in 1989.

events.event_description: Son Marston born
events.evidence_text: Son Marston Glenn was born in 1990.

events.event_description: Son Cooper born
events.evidence_text: Son Cooper was born in 1991.

events.event_description: Separates from Kimberley Conrad (divorce final 2010)
events.evidence_text: He separated from Conrad in 1998; divorce finalized in 2010.

events.event_description: Marries Crystal Harris
events.evidence_text: He married Crystal Harris on December 31, 2012.

events.event_description: Marries Elizabeth Higgins
events.evidence_text: DeLorean married Elizabeth Higgins in September 1954.

events.event_description: Joins Pontiac division of General Motors
events.evidence_text: He joined GM's Pontiac division in 1956.

events.event_description: Pontiac GTO debuts, credited as first muscle car
events.evidence_text: The GTO debuted in 1964 as a Tempest/LeMans option package.

events.event_description: Promoted to general manager of Pontiac
events.evidence_text: He was promoted to head of the Pontiac division in 1965.

events.event_description: Named head of Chevrolet division
events.evidence_text: In February 1969 he was promoted to run Chevrolet.

events.event_description: Divorces Elizabeth Higgins; marries Kelly Harmon (May 31)
events.evidence_text: First marriage ended 1969; he married Kelly Harmon May 31, 1969.

events.event_description: Announces departure from General Motors
events.evidence_text: He announced his departure from GM on April 2, 1973.

events.event_description: Founds DeLorean Motor Company; marries Cristina Ferrare
events.evidence_text: He founded DeLorean Motor Company and married Cristina Ferrare in 1973.

events.event_description: DMC DeLorean sports car reaches consumers
events.evidence_text: The DMC DeLorean reached the consumer market in January 1981.

events.event_description: DeLorean Motor Company and Belfast factory placed in receivership
events.evidence_text: DMC and its Dunmurry factory went into receivership in February 1982.

events.event_description: Arrested in FBI cocaine-trafficking sting
events.evidence_text: He was charged with cocaine trafficking after an FBI sting.

events.event_description: Acquitted of drug-trafficking charges (entrapment defense)
events.evidence_text: A jury found him not guilty of trafficking on August 16, 1984.

events.event_description: Divorces Cristina Ferrare; indicted for fraud Sept 1985 (later acquitted)
events.evidence_text: Ferrare divorce in 1985; fraud indictment September 1985, later acquitted.

events.event_description: Declares personal bankruptcy; forced to sell New Jersey estate in 2000
events.evidence_text: He declared personal bankruptcy in 1999 and sold his Bedminster estate.

events.event_description: Daughter born to Sally Baldwin; marries Baldwin in 2002
events.evidence_text: A daughter was born to Sally Baldwin in 2002; they married.

events.event_description: Marries attorney Leo Panzirer
events.evidence_text: She married first husband Leo Panzirer in 1938.

events.event_description: Divorces Leo Panzirer
events.evidence_text: Her marriage to Panzirer ended in divorce in 1952.

events.event_description: Joins Brown Harris Stevens as senior vice-president
events.evidence_text: She joined Harry Helmsley's firm Brown Harris Stevens as senior VP.

events.event_description: Tenants win suit over forced condo purchases; real estate license suspended
events.evidence_text: Tenants sued and won; her real estate license was suspended.

events.event_description: Marries real estate magnate Harry Helmsley
events.evidence_text: She married Harry Helmsley on April 8, 1972.

events.event_description: Becomes public face of Helmsley Hotels ad campaign, running the hotel chain
events.evidence_text: She ran Harry's hotel empire, controlling 23 hotels by 1989.

events.event_description: Indicted with Harry Helmsley on federal tax evasion and extortion charges
events.evidence_text: U.S. Attorney Giuliani indicted the Helmsleys on tax and extortion charges.

events.event_description: Convicted of federal tax evasion and fraud (acquitted of extortion)
events.evidence_text: Convicted August 30, 1989 on tax and fraud counts.

events.event_description: Sentenced to four years in prison and $7.1 million fine
events.evidence_text: She received a four-year sentence and multimillion-dollar fine.

events.event_description: Reports to federal prison
events.evidence_text: She was ordered to report to prison April 15, 1992.

events.event_description: Released from federal custody
events.evidence_text: She was released from custody on January 26, 1994.

events.event_description: Inherits Harry Helmsley's fortune on his death
events.evidence_text: Harry died in 1997, leaving her his fortune.

events.event_description: Jury awards $11.2 million to fired employee in discrimination suit (later reduced)
events.evidence_text: Jury awarded ex-employee $11.2 million, later cut to $554,000.

events.event_description: Marries Lori Hackel; graduates UC Berkeley
events.evidence_text: He graduated from Berkeley and married Lori Hackel in 1968.

events.event_description: Moves Drexel high-yield bond operation to Century City, Los Angeles
events.evidence_text: He relocated Drexel's high-yield bond department to Los Angeles in 1978.

events.event_description: Peak Drexel compensation; earnings exceeded $1 billion over four years
events.evidence_text: His late-1980s compensation exceeded $1 billion over four years.

events.event_description: Implicated by Ivan Boesky's guilty plea, triggering SEC and criminal probes
events.evidence_text: Boesky's plea implicated Milken, prompting SEC and criminal investigations.

events.event_description: Indicted on 98 counts of racketeering and securities fraud
events.evidence_text: A federal grand jury indicted Milken on 98 counts in March 1989.

events.event_description: Leaves Drexel Burnham Lambert
events.evidence_text: Milken departed Drexel in 1989 after his indictment.

events.event_description: Pleads guilty to six counts; agrees to about $600 million in fines and settlements
events.evidence_text: He pleaded guilty to six securities and tax counts in April 1990.

events.event_description: Sentenced to ten years in prison (later reduced to two)
events.evidence_text: Sentenced to ten years, later reduced; he served 22 months.

events.event_description: Released from prison; diagnosed with prostate cancer the same month
events.evidence_text: Released in 1993, then diagnosed with prostate cancer that month.

events.event_description: Founds Prostate Cancer Foundation (philanthropy career)
events.evidence_text: He founded the Prostate Cancer Foundation after his diagnosis.

events.event_description: Co-founds Knowledge Universe education company with brother Lowell
events.evidence_text: He co-founded Knowledge Universe with his brother in 1996.

events.event_description: SEC investigates possible violation of his lifetime securities-industry ban
events.evidence_text: SEC announced a probe into whether he breached his lifetime ban.

events.event_description: Receives full presidential pardon from Donald Trump
events.evidence_text: Trump granted Milken a full pardon on February 18, 2020.

events.event_description: Marries Byun Joong-seok
events.evidence_text: He married Byun Joong-seok after meeting her in late 1935.

events.event_description: Takes over a rice store, renamed Kyungil Rice Store
events.evidence_text: A store owner handed him the rice shop, renamed Kyungil.

events.event_description: Loses rice store under colonial rice-trade restrictions
events.evidence_text: Colonial controls on Korean rice shops cost him the store.

events.event_description: Starts A-do Service auto repair garage with borrowed 3,000 won
events.evidence_text: He started A-do Service Garage in Seoul with a loan.

events.event_description: A-do Service garage destroyed by fire
events.evidence_text: The A-do Service factory burned down in 1941.

events.event_description: Garage forcibly merged into a steel plant by colonial authorities
events.evidence_text: Authorities forced the garage into a merger; he returned home.

events.event_description: Founds Hyundai Togeon (construction), after Hyundai Auto Service in 1946
events.evidence_text: He founded Hyundai Auto Service in 1946 and Hyundai Togeon in 1947.

events.event_description: Founds Hyundai Motor Company
events.evidence_text: Hyundai Motor Company was established in December 1967.

events.event_description: Founds Hyundai shipbuilding (Ulsan shipyard), later Hyundai Heavy Industries
events.evidence_text: He founded Hyundai Shipbuilding with headquarters at the Ulsan shipyard.

events.event_description: Hyundai Construction wins Jubail Industrial Harbour contract in Saudi Arabia (~$930M)
events.evidence_text: Hyundai won the Jubail harbour project, Korea's landmark overseas contract.

events.event_description: Hyundai Pony, Korea's first mass-produced domestic car, introduced
events.evidence_text: He introduced the Hyundai Pony in 1976.

events.event_description: Leads successful bid for the 1988 Seoul Olympics
events.evidence_text: Seoul's 1988 Olympic bid was confirmed in 1981 under his leadership.

events.event_description: Steps back to honorary chairman of Hyundai Group
events.evidence_text: He became honorary chairman of Hyundai Group in February 1987.

events.event_description: Runs for president as Unification National Party candidate, finishes third
events.evidence_text: He ran for president in 1992 and finished third.

events.event_description: Crosses into North Korea with 500 cattle via Panmunjom
events.evidence_text: He crossed to North Korea with 500 head of cattle in June 1998.

events.event_description: Eldest daughter Kim Sun-jung born
events.evidence_text: Eldest daughter Kim Sun-jung was born in September 1965.

events.event_description: Founds Daewoo Industrial textile trading firm with 5 million won
events.evidence_text: He co-founded Daewoo Industrial in March 1967 with 5 million won.

events.event_description: Eldest son Kim Sun-jae born
events.evidence_text: Eldest son Kim Sun-jae was born in January 1967.

events.event_description: Becomes president and CEO of Daewoo Industrial
events.evidence_text: He took office as Daewoo Industrial president in 1970.

events.event_description: Daewoo Corporation launched; becomes Daewoo Group chairman
events.evidence_text: Daewoo Corporation launched in 1982 with him as group chairman.

events.event_description: Memoir "The World Is Wide and There Is Much to Do" sells over a million copies
events.evidence_text: His 1989 essay book sold over a million copies in six months.

events.event_description: Becomes chairman of the Federation of Korean Industries
events.evidence_text: He became chairman of the Federation of Korean Industries in 1998.

events.event_description: Daewoo liquidity crisis erupts after Asian financial crisis
events.evidence_text: A late-1998 broker report triggered Daewoo's deepening crisis.

events.event_description: Daewoo Group collapses with about $50 billion debt; resigns as chairman
events.evidence_text: Daewoo went bankrupt with about $50 billion in debt; he stepped down.

events.event_description: Leaves Korea, living abroad for about five years to avoid prosecution
events.evidence_text: He fled abroad, mainly Vietnam, for nearly six years.

events.event_description: Arrested on return to South Korea
events.evidence_text: He was arrested after returning to Korea on June 14, 2005.

events.event_description: Convicted of embezzlement and accounting fraud; 10-year sentence (8.5 years on appeal)
events.evidence_text: Sentenced to ten years for fraud, reduced to 8.5 on appeal.

events.event_description: Appeal court confirms forfeiture of about 17.9 trillion won
events.evidence_text: Appeal ruling ordered forfeiture of roughly 17.9 trillion won.

events.event_description: Receives special presidential pardon
events.evidence_text: President Roh Moo-hyun granted him a special pardon.
